segments.en: Muse, sing of Hermes, the son of Zeus and Maia, lord of Cyllene and Arcadia rich in flocks, the luck-bringing messenger of the immortals whom Maia bare, the rich-tressed nymph, when she was joined in love with Zeus, —a shy goddess, for she avoided the company of the blessed gods, and lived within a deep, shady cave. There the son of Cronos used to lie with the rich-tressed nymph, unseen by deathless gods and mortal men, at dead of night while sweet sleep should hold white-armed Hera fast. And when the purpose of great Zeus was fulfilled, and the tenth moon with her was fixed in heaven, she was delivered and a notable thing was come to pass. For then she bare a son, of many shifts, blandly cunning, a robber, a cattle driver, a bringer of dreams, a watcher by night, a thief at the gates, one who was soon to show forth wonderful deeds among the deathless gods. Born with the dawning, at mid-day he played on the lyre, and in the evening he stole the cattle of far-shooting Apollo on the fourth day of the month; for on that day queenly Maia bare him.
segments.zh: 繆斯啊，請唱頌赫爾墨斯——宙斯與瑪亞之子，基勒涅的主人，羊群豐饒的阿卡狄亞的主人，幸運的使者，永恆者的傳令官，是秀髮的寧芙瑪亞所生，她在與宙斯的愛欲相合時孕育了他。這是一位害羞的女神，她迴避了至福神祇的聚會，獨自住在深邃而陰暗的洞窟裡。克洛諾斯之子常在那裡，在不為長生的神祇與凡人所見之處，與秀髮的寧芙相歡，趁著夜深，當甜蜜的睡眠籠罩白臂赫拉之時。當大宙斯的目的得以成全，第十個月亮也隨之在天空中固定，她分娩了，一樁不尋常的事由此而生。她生下了一個兒子，多機變者，巧言者，盜賊，牧牛人，夢之使者，夜間的守望者，門邊的竊賊——他將很快在永恆的神祇們面前展現奇妙的功績。生於黎明時分，正午時他彈起了琴，到了傍晚他竊取了遠射阿波羅的牛群，在月月四日之際；因為就在那天高貴的瑪亞生下了他。

segments.en: So soon as he had leaped from his mother's heavenly womb, he lay not long waiting in his holy cradle, but he sprang up and sought the oxen of Apollo. But as he stepped over the threshold of the high-roofed cave, he found a tortoise there and gained endless delight. For it was Hermes who first made the tortoise a singer. The creature fell in his way at the courtyard gate, where it was feeding on the rich grass before the dwelling, waddling along. When he saw it, the luck-bringing son of Zeus laughed and said: “An omen of great luck for me so soon! I do not slight it. Hail, comrade of the feast, lovely in shape, sounding at the dance! With joy I meet you! Where got you that rich gaud for covering, that spangled shell —a tortoise living in the mountains? But I will take and carry you within: you shall help me and I will do you no disgrace, though first of all you must profit me. It is better to be at home: harm may come out of doors. Living, you shall be a spell against mischievous witchcraftPliny notices the efficacy of the flesh of a tortoise against witchcraft. In Geoponica i. 14. 8 the living tortoise is prescribed as a charm to preserve vineyards from hail.; but if you die, then you shall make sweetest song.” Thus speaking, he took up the tortoise in both hands
segments.zh: 他一旦從母親的天上子宮中躍出，並不在聖潔的搖籃中久待，而是立刻跳起身來，尋找阿波羅的牛群。但當他踏過高屋頂洞穴的門檻時，他發現了一隻烏龜，於是得到了無盡的歡喜。蓋是赫爾墨斯首先讓烏龜成為歌手。這生物擋在他去路上，在住處前面的院子門口，在茂密的草叢中爬行著進食。他看見它，幸運之神宙斯之子笑著說：「對我來說，這是一個極大幸運的徵兆，來得真是時候！我不輕視它。問好，宴席的伴侶啊，形態可愛者，舞樂中發出聲音者！我歡喜與你相遇！你那華麗的裝飾在何處得來，那繁星般的殼——住在山裡的烏龜？但我要把你帶進去：你會幫助我，而我也不會使你蒙羞，儘管首先你必須對我有益。住在家裡更好：在外面可能遭禍。活著時，你將是抵禦惡毒巫術的符咒；但若你死了，那你就能唱出最甜蜜的歌聲。」說罷這些話，他用雙手托起了烏龜

segments.en: and went back into the house carrying his charming toy. Then he cut off its limbs and scooped out the marrow of the mountain-tortoise with a scoop of grey iron. As a swift thought darts through the heart of a man when thronging cares haunt him, or as bright glances flash from the eye, so glorious Hermes planned both thought and deed at once. He cut stalks of reed to measure and fixed them, fastening their ends across the back and through the shell of the tortoise, and then stretched ox hide all over it by his skill. Also he put in the horns and fitted a cross-piece upon the two of them, and stretched seven strings of sheep-gut. But when he had made it he proved each string in turn with the key, as he held the lovely thing. At the touch of his hand it sounded marvelously; and, as he tried it, the god sang sweet random snatches, even as youths bandy taunts at festivals. He sang of Zeus the son of Cronos and neat-shod Maia, the converse which they had before in the comradeship of love, telling all the glorious tale of his own begetting.
segments.zh: 回到屋裡，帶著他心愛的玩具。然後他割下了它的四肢，用灰色鐵勺掏空了山烏龜的骨髓。如同急速的思想閃現在被眾多憂慮困擾之人的心中，又如明亮的光芒從眼睛迸出，如此光榮的赫爾墨斯一下子同時籌畫了念想與行動。他截取蘆葦莖稈調好尺寸，把它們固定下來，在烏龜的背部和殼上貫穿，然後用牛皮以他的手藝蒙住了一切。他還安上了角，在兩角之間裝上了一根橫木，繃上了七根羊腸弦。但當他造好它時，他逐一試撥每根弦，手持著這可愛的東西。在他手指的觸摸下，它發出了奇妙的聲音；當他試彈時，這位神祇唱起了甜蜜的隨意歌調，正如少年們在節慶上互相嘲笑一樣。他唱頌克洛諾斯之子宙斯和穿著整潔靴子的瑪亞，他們在愛欲的親密中曾有過的交流，述說著他自己誕生的全部光榮故事。

segments.en: He celebrated, too, the handmaids of the nymph, and her bright home, and the tripods all about the house, and the abundant cauldrons.But while he was singing of all these, his heart was bent on other matters. And he took the hollow lyre and laid it in his sacred cradle, and sprang from the sweet-smelling hall to a watch-place, pondering sheer trickery in his heart —deeds such as knavish folk pursue in the dark night-time; for he longed to taste flesh. The Sun was going down beneath the earth towards Ocean with his horses and chariot when Hermes came hurrying to the shadowy mountains of Pieria, where the divine cattle of the blessed gods had their steads and grazed the pleasant, unmown meadows. Of these the Son of Maia, the sharp-eyed slayer of Argus then cut off from the herd fifty loud-lowing kine, and drove them straggling-wise across a sandy place, turning their hoof-prints aside. Also, he bethought him of a crafty ruse and reversed the marks of their hoofs, making the front behind and the hind before, while he himself walked the other way.Hermes makes the cattle walk backwards way, so that they seem to be going towards the meadow instead of leaving it (cp. 1. 345); he himself walks in the normal manner, relying on his sandals as a disguise. Then he wove sandals with wicker-work by the sand of the sea,
segments.zh: 他也讚美了仙女的侍女們，她光明的家宅，四處的鼎，和豐沛的大釜。但當他唱著這一切時，他的心卻轉向別處。他取過中空的琴，放入神聖的搖籃，從芬芳的殿堂躍出，來到了監視之所，心中思謀著純粹的詭計——那是暗夜中狡黠之徒所為的行為；因為他渴望嚐到血肉。太陽正駕著馬和戰車往地下、往俄刻阿諾斯沉去時，赫爾墨斯匆匆趕往幽暗的皮埃里亞山區，那裡有蒙福的眾神的聖牛群作為棲所，在宜人、未割的草地上放牧。瑪亞之子、目光銳利的殺死阿爾戈斯的那位，就從牛群中掠出五十頭高聲哞叫的母牛，驅趕它們橫跨沙地，掉轉了它們的足印。他也想到了狡猾之計，反轉了牲畜足印的痕跡，使前面的在後面，後面的在前面，而他自己則往另一方向行走。然後他在海邊的沙地上用柳條編織涼鞋，

segments.en: wonderful things, unthought of, unimagined; for he mixed together tamarisk and myrtle-twigs, fastening together an armful of their fresh, young wood, and tied them, leaves and all securely under his feet as light sandals. That brushwood the glorious Slayer of Argus plucked in Pieria as he was preparing for his journey, making shiftSuch seems to be the meaning indicated by the context, though the verb is taken by Allen and Sikes to mean, “to be like oneself,” and so “to be original.” as one making haste for a long journey. segments.zh: 奇妙之物，前所未想，前所未聞；他將檵木和桃金孃的枝條混在一起，把一抱新的、嫩的木材紮緊，將葉子和一切都牢牢綁在腳下作為輕便的涼鞋。光輝的殺死阿爾戈斯的那位在皮埃里亞采下這灌木叢，為他的旅程作準備，匆促行動如同一人在匆忙遠行。但一位老人在翻耕盛花的葡萄園時，看見了他從平原匆匆而下經過多草的翁刻斯托斯。於是瑪亞之子開口說道：「老人啊，腰彎著耕作你的葡萄藤，當這一切都結實時，經過許多幽暗的山區、迴盪的峽谷和花開的平原，光輝的赫爾墨斯驅趕著牲畜前行，那時你必有豐沛的葡萄酒。而今神聖的夜晚，他的暗助力，大部已逝，啟動眾人勞作的曙光迫近，而光明的塞勒涅，

segments.en: Then he went on from task to task: first he cut up the rich, fatted meat, and pierced it with wooden spits, and roasted flesh and the honorable chine and the paunch full of dark blood all together. He laid them there upon the ground, and spread out the hides on a rugged rock: and so they are still there many ages afterwards, a long, long time after all this, and are continuallyO. Muller thinks the “hides” were a stalactite formation in the “Cave of Nestor” near Messenian Pylos, —though the cave of Hermes is near the Alpheus (1. 139). Others suggest that actual skins were shown as relics before some cave near Triphylian Pylos.. Next glad-hearted Hermes dragged the rich meats he had prepared and put them on a smooth, flat stone, and divided them into twelve portions distributed by lot, making each portion wholly honorable. Then glorious Hermes longed for the sacrificial meat, for the sweet savour wearied him, god though he was; nevertheless his proud heart was not prevailed upon to devour the flesh, although he greatly desired.Gemoll explains that Hermes, having offered all the meat as sacrifice to the Twelve Gods, remembers that he himself as one of them must be content with the savour instead of the substance of the sacrifice. Can it be that by eating he would have forfeited the position he claimed as one of the Twelve Gods? But he put away in the high-roofed byre the fat and all the flesh, placing them high up to be a token of his youthful theft. And after that he gathered dry sticks and utterly destroyed with fire all the hoofs and all the heads. And when the god had duly finished all, he threw his sandals into deep-eddying Alpheus,

segments.en: and quenched the embers, covering the black ashes with sand, and so spent the night while Selene's soft light shone down. Then the god went straight back again at dawn to the bright crests of Cyllene, and no one met him on the long journey either of the blessed gods or mortal men, nor did any dog bark. And luck-bringing Hermes, the son of Zeus, passed edgeways through the key-hole of the hall like the autumn breeze, even as mist: straight through the cave he went and came to the rich inner chamber, walking softly, and making no noise as one might upon the floor. Then glorious Hermes went hurriedly to his cradle, wrapping his swaddling clothes about his shoulders as though he were a feeble babe, and lay playing with the covering about his knees; but at his left hand he kept close his sweet lyre. But the god did not pass unseen by the goddess his mother; but she said to him: “How now, you rogue! Whence come you back so at night-time, you that wear shamelessness as a garment? And now I surely believe the son of Leto will soon have you forth out of doors with unbreakable cords about your ribs, or you will live a rogue's life in the glens robbing by whiles.

Nay, but I will try whatever plan is best, and so feed myself and you continually. We will not be content to remain here, as you bid, alone of all the gods unfee'd with offerings and prayers. Better to live in fellowship with the deathless gods continually, rich, wealthy, and enjoying stores of grain, than to sit always in a gloomy cave: and, as regards honor, I too will enter upon the rite that Apollo has. If my father will not give it me, I will seek —and I am able —to be a prince of robbers. And if Leto's most glorious son shall seek me out, I think another and a greater loss will befall him. However, I was digging about my plot of vineyard all day long until the sun went down, and I thought, good sir, but I do not know for certain, that I marked a child, whoever the child was, that followed long-horned cattle— an infant who had a staff and kept walking from side to side: he was driving them backwards way, with their heads towards him.” So said the old man. And when Apollo heard this report, he went yet more quickly on his way, and presently, seeing a long-winged bird, he knew at once by that omen that the thief was the child of Zeus the son of Cronos. So the lord Apollo, son of Zeus, hurried on to goodly Pylos seeking his shambling oxen, and he had his broad shoulders covered with a dark cloud. But when the Far-Shooter perceived the tracks, he cried: “Oh, oh! Truly this is a great marvel that my eyes behold!
segments.zh: 老人答他說：「我的孩子，要說出眼睛看見的一切是困難的；因為許多旅人經常在這路上來來往往，有些懷著很多壞念頭，有些則懷著善意：很難認出每一個人。不過，我整天在我的葡萄園地裡挖掘，直到太陽下山，我想，好先生，但我不確定，我好像看到了一個孩子，不管那孩子是誰，他跟在長角的牛後面——一個嬰兒，拿著一根木杖，不停地左右走動：他在把它們趕回來，頭朝著他的方向。」老人這樣說。阿波羅聽到這報告，他更加急速地趕路，不久，他看到一隻長翅膀的鳥，他立刻從那預兆認出了小偷是克洛諾斯之子宙斯的孩子。所以主神阿波羅，宙斯之子，匆忙趕往美麗的皮洛斯去尋他搖晃的牛群，他寬闊的肩膀被一片烏雲所覆蓋。但當遠射者察覺到蹤跡時，他大聲疾呼：「哦，哦！真的，這是我眼睛看到的大奇蹟！

segments.en: These are indeed the tracks of straight-horned oxen, but they are turned backwards towards the flowery meadow. But these others are not the footprints of man or woman or grey wolves or bears or lions, nor do I think they are the tracks of a rough-maned Centaur — whoever it be that with swift feet makes such monstrous footprints; wonderful are the tracks on this side of the way, but yet more wonderful are those on that.” When he had so said, the lord Apollo, the Son of Zeus hastened on and came to the forest-clad mountain of Cyllene and the deep-shadowed cave in the rock where the divine nymph brought forth the child of Zeus who is the son of Cronos. A sweet odor spread over the lovely hill, and many thin-shanked sheep were grazing on the grass. Then far-shooting Apollo himself stepped down in haste over the stone threshold into the dusky cave. Now when the Son of Zeus and Maia saw Apollo in a rage about his cattle, he snuggled down in his fragrant swaddling-clothes; and as wood-ash covers over the deep embers of tree-stumps, so Hermes cuddled himself up when he saw the Far-Shooter.
segments.zh: 這些確實是直角牛的蹤跡，但它們掉轉向著花開的草地。但這些其他的卻不是人或婦女或灰狼或熊或獅子的足跡，我也不認為它們是毛髮蓬亂的人馬的蹤跡——不管是誰用輕快的雙腳留下這樣怪異的足印；這一邊的蹤跡是奇異的，但那一邊的更加奇異。」他說完這些話，主神阿波羅，宙斯之子，加快步伐，來到森林密布的基勒涅山和深暗的岩洞，那裡是神聖的仙女生下宙斯的孩子——克洛諾斯之子的地方。甜蜜的香氣飄散在可愛的山丘上，許多細腿的綿羊在草地上吃草。遠射的阿波羅本人急速踏過石頭門檻走進陰暗的洞穴。當宙斯之子與美亞的兒子看到阿波羅為了他的牛而怒火中燒，他就蜷縮在他芬芳的襁褓裡；就像木灰覆蓋樹樁深處的餘燼，赫爾墨斯在看到遠射者時就把自己蜷縮起來了。

segments.en: He squeezed head and hands and feet together in a small space, like a new born child seeking sweet sleep, though in truth he was wide awake, and he kept his lyre under his armpit. But the Son of Leto was aware and failed not to perceive the beautiful mountain-nymph and her dear son, albeit a little child and swathed so craftily. He peered in every corner of the great dwelling and, taking a bright key, he opened three closets full of nectar and lovely ambrosia. And much gold and silver was stored in them, and many garments of the nymph, some purple and some silvery white, such as are kept in the sacred houses of the blessed gods. Then, after the Son of Leto had searched out the recesses of the great house, he spake to glorious Hermes: “Child, lying in the cradle, make haste and tell me of my cattle, or we two will soon fall out angrily. For I will take and cast you into dusky Tartarus and awful hopeless darkness, and neither your mother nor your father shall free you or bring you up again to the light, but you will wander under the earth and be the leader amongst little folk.”Hermes is ambitious (1.175), but if he is cast into Hades he will have to be content with the leadership of mere babies like himself, since those in Hades retain the state of growth —whether childhood or manhood —in which they are at the moment of leaving the upper world.
segments.zh: 他把頭、手、腳擠在狹小的空間裡，如同新生的嬰兒尋求甜蜜的睡眠，然而實際上他是完全清醒的，並把竪琴夾在腋下。但勒托之子察覺到了，並未曾忽視那美麗的山林女仙和她親愛的兒子，雖然他還是個小孩子，裹得如此巧妙。他窺探了宏偉住宅的每個角落，拿起明亮的鑰匙，打開了三只盛滿琼漿與美妙神仙食物的貯物間。其中儲藏著許多黃金與白銀，還有許多山林女仙的衣袍，有紫色的，也有銀白色的，正如聖潔的福祉之神的聖殿中保存的那樣。於是勒托之子搜遍了宏偉住宅的隱秘處後，對光輝的赫爾墨斯說道：「小孩，躺在搖籃裡，快說吧，告訴我我的牛群在哪裡，否則我倆將很快怒而相爭。我會把你抓住，扔進昏暗的塔爾塔羅斯和可怖的無望之黑暗中，你的母親和父親都救不了你，也不會再把你帶回光明中，而你將在地下流浪，做小人物的領袖。」（赫爾墨斯有雄心壯志（1.175），但若他被扔入哈得斯，他就只能甘心領導那些與他一樣的嬰孩了，因為哈得斯中的人保持著他們離開上界時的成長狀態——無論是童年還是成年。）

segments.en: Then Hermes answered him with crafty words: “Son of Leto, what harsh words are these you have spoken? And is it cattle of the field you are come here to seek? I have not seen them: I have not heard of them: no one has told me of them. I cannot give news of them, nor win the reward for news. Am I like a cattle-lifter, a stalwart person? This is no task for me: rather I care for other things: I care for sleep, and milk of my mother's breast, and wrappings round my shoulders, and warm baths. Let no one hear the cause of this dispute; for this would be a great marvel indeed among the deathless gods, that a child newly born should pass in through the forepart of the house with cattle of the field: herein you speak extravagantly. I was born yesterday, and my feet are soft and the ground beneath is rough; nevertheless, if you will have it so, I will swear a great oath by my father's head and vow that neither am I guilty myself, neither have I seen any other who stole your cows —whatever cows may be; for I know them only by hearsay.” So, then, said Hermes, shooting quick glances from his eyes: and he kept raising his brows and looking this way and that,
segments.zh: 於是赫爾墨斯用狡詐的言辭回答他說：「勒托之子啊，你說出的這些言辭多麼苛刻啊？你來這裡是為了尋找田野裡的牛群嗎？我沒有看見過它們，我沒有聽說過它們，沒有人告訴過我它們的事。我無法提供它們的消息，也贏不了報信的獎賞。我看起來像一個牛賊，一個壯漢嗎？這不是我的工作：我關心的是其他事物：我關心睡眠，母親乳房裡的奶水，肩膀上的襁褓，還有溫暖的浴水。不要讓任何人聽到這場爭執的原因；因為在不朽的諸神中，這將是一件大奇事，一個新生的嬰孩竟能從房屋前方進來，帶著田野裡的牛群：你在這點上說得太過分了。我昨天才出生，我的腳還很柔軟，而我腳下的地面很粗糙；然而，若你非要這樣，我會以父親的頭為誓起重誓，發誓說既不是我本人偷了你的牛，也沒見過任何別人偷你的牛——不管那些牛是什麼；因為我只是聽說過它們。」於是赫爾墨斯這樣說著，眼睛發出敏捷的光芒：他不斷揚起眉毛，眼光向四面轉移，

segments.en: whistling long and listening to Apollo's story as to an idle tale. But far-working Apollo laughed softly and said to him: “O rogue, deceiver, crafty in heart, you talk so innocently that I most surely believe that you have broken into many a well-built house and stripped more than one poor wretch bare this night, Literally, “you have made him sit on the floor,” i.e. “you have stolen everything down to his last chair.” gathering his goods together all over the house without noise. You will plague many a lonely herdsman in mountain glades, when you come on herds and thick-fleeced sheep, and have a hankering after flesh. But come now, if you would not sleep your last and latest sleep, get out of your cradle, you comrade of dark night. Surely hereafter this shall be your title amongst the deathless gods, to be called the prince of robbers continually.” So said Phoebus Apollo, and took the child and began to carry him. But at that moment the strong Slayer of Argus had his plan, and, while Apollo held him in his hands, sent forth an omen, a hard-worked belly-serf, a rude messenger, and sneezed directly after. And when Apollo heard it, he dropped glorious Hermes out of his hands on the ground:
segments.zh: 吹著長長的口哨，把阿波羅的故事當作無聊的閒談來聽。但遠射的阿波羅輕聲笑了，對他說道：「哦，你這調皮鬼、欺騙者、心思狡詐的傢伙，你說得那麼天真無邪，我最確信你已經闖進了許多堅固的房屋，今夜剝奪了不少可憐人（字面上是「讓他坐在地板上」，即「你把他的一切都偷走了，連最後一把椅子都沒放過」），把他的東西無聲地聚集在整個房屋裡。當你來到牲畜和厚毛羊羣之處時，你將折磨許多孤獨的牧人在山林空地裡，而且渴望肉食。但來吧，如果你不想睡最後一次也是最終的睡眠，就從搖籃裡爬出來吧，你這黑夜的夥伴。確實，此後你將在不朽的諸神中獲得一個頭銜，被稱為盜賊的王子，永遠不變。」斐波斯阿波羅這樣說著，拿起了這小孩，開始帶他走。但就在那時，強大的殺死阿爾戈斯者有了主意，在阿波羅把他握在手中時，送出了一個徵兆——一個辛苦勞作的肚子奴隸，一個粗魯的信使——直接打了個噴嚏。阿波羅聽到時，就把光輝的赫爾墨斯從手中扔在地上：

segments.en: then sitting down before him, though he was eager to go on his way, he spoke mockingly to Hermes: “Fear not, little swaddling baby, son of Zeus and Maia. I shall find the strong cattle presently by these omens, and you shall lead the way.” When Apollo had so said, Cyllenian Hermes sprang up quickly, starting in haste. With both hands he pushed up to his ears the covering that he had wrapped about his shoulders, and said: “Where are you carrying me, Far-Worker, hastiest of all the gods? Is it because of your cattle that you are so angry and harass me? O dear, would that all the sort of oxen might perish; for it is not I who stole your cows, nor did I see another steal them —whatever cows may be, and of that I have only heard report. Nay, give right and take it before Zeus, the Son of Cronos.” So Hermes the shepherd and Leto's glorious son kept stubbornly disputing each article of their quarrel: Apollo, speaking truly not unfairly sought to seize glorious Hermes because of the cows; but he, the Cyllenian, tried to deceive the God of the Silver Bow with tricks and cunning words. But when, though he had many wiles, he found the other had as many shifts,
segments.zh: 於是他在赫爾墨斯面前坐下，雖然心急欲往，卻嘲笑著說：「莫懼，小小襁褓兒，宙斯與邁亞之子。我很快就會循這些徵兆尋到那強壯的牲畜，你要為我帶路。」阿波羅說罷，基勒涅的赫爾墨斯倏地躍起，急匆匆地動身。他用雙手把裹在肩上的布推至耳邊，說道：「遠射者啊，你要帶我去哪裡？眾神中最急躁的你，這是為了你的牲畜而如此震怒、騷擾我嗎？天哪，要是所有那種牛都消亡就好了；因為不是我偷了你的牛，我也沒看見別人偷——那些牛無論如何，我也只是聽說罷了。不，你去克洛諾斯之子宙斯那裡講理、起訴吧。」於是牧人赫爾墨斯與勒托光榮的兒子就為爭執的每一項條款頑強地爭論著：阿波羅以真摯與公正的態度，想要為那些牛逮住光榮的赫爾墨斯；但基勒涅人卻試圖用詭計與巧言來欺騙銀弓之神。然而當他多般詭計在握，卻發現對方也有許多應變之策，

segments.en: he began to walk across the sand, himself in front, while the Son of Zeus and Leto came behind. Soon they came, these lovely children of Zeus, to the top of fragrant Olympus, to their father, the Son of Cronos; for there were the scales of judgement set for them both. There was an assembly on snowy Olympus, and the immortals who perish not were gathering after the hour of gold-throned Dawn. Then Hermes and Apollo of the Silver Bow stood at the knees of Zeus: and Zeus who thunders on high spoke to his glorious son and asked him: “Phoebus, whence come you driving this great spoil, a child new born that has the look of a herald? This is a weighty matter that is come before the council of the gods.” Then the lord, far-working Apollo, answered him: “O my father, you shall soon hear no trifling tale though you reproach me that I alone am fond of spoil. Here is a child, a burgling robber, whom I found after a long journey in the hills of Cyllene: for my part I have never seen one so pert either among the gods or all men that catch folk unawares throughout the world.
segments.zh: 他就開始走過沙地，他自己在前，宙斯與勒托之子隨在後。很快，宙斯這兩位可愛的兒女就來到了香氣馥郁的奧林匹斯山頂，來到他們的父親克洛諾斯之子那裡；因為在那裡為他們兩人設置了天秤。雪白的奧林匹斯山上聚集著一個大會，金座的晨曦女神之時過後，不朽不死的神聖存在們都聚集了。於是赫爾墨斯與銀弓的阿波羅站在宙斯的膝前：雷鳴的宙斯向他光榮的兒子說話，問他：「福波斯啊，你驅趕著這般龐大的贓物而來，那是個新生的嬰孩，看起來像個傳令官——這是一樁沉重的事務來到了諸神的議會。」於是遠射的主人阿波羅答道：「父親啊，你很快就會聽到絕非瑣事的故事，雖然你責備我獨獨喜愛贓物。這是個嬰孩，一個行竊的盜賊，我在基勒涅山中長途跋涉後發現了他：就我而言，我從未見過這樣無禮的傢伙，無論在眾神之中，還是在所有那些遍布世界去偷襲他人的人當中。

segments.en: He stole away my cows from their meadow and drove them off in the evening along the shore of the loud-roaring sea, making straight for Pylos. There were double tracks, and wonderful they were, such as one might marvel at, the doing of a clever sprite; for as for the cows, the dark dust kept and showed their footprints leading towards the flowery meadow; but he himself —bewildering creature —crossed the sandy ground outside the path, not on his feet nor yet on his hands; but, furnished with some other means he trudged his way —wonder of wonders! —as though one walked on slender oak-trees. Now while he followed the cattle across sandy ground, all the tracks showed quite clearly in the dust; but when he had finished the long way across the sand, presently the cows' track and his own could not be traced over the hard ground. But a mortal man noticed him as he drove the wide-browed kine straight towards Pylos. And as soon as he had shut them up quietly, and had gone home by crafty turns and twists, he lay down in his cradle in the gloom of a dim cave, as still as dark night, so that not even
segments.zh: 他從牧場偷走了我的牲畜，在傍晚沿著轟鳴的大海之濱趕著它們離去，直奔皮洛斯。有著雙重的足跡，真是奇異至極，足令人驚嘆，那是個聰慧的小精靈的傑作；至於那些牛，黑色的塵埃保留著並顯示了它們的足跡通向花海草地；但他自己——那迷人的傢伙——走過沙地遠離了小徑，不是用腳也不是用手；而是配著某種別的手段他跋涉著——奇蹟中的奇蹟！——就像有人踩著細橡樹行走一樣。現在當他跟隨牲畜走過沙地時，所有的足跡都在塵埃中清晰可見；但當他走完了漫長的沙地路程後，很快地那些牛的足跡與他的足跡就在硬地上無法追尋了。然而一個凡人發現了他，當他驅趕著闊額的牲畜直奔皮洛斯時。等到他安靜地把它們關好，並已轉著彎曲之路回到了家，他就躺在了昏暗洞穴內的搖籃裡，靜寂得如暗夜一般，以至於

segments.en: an eagle keenly gazing would have spied him. Much he rubbed his eyes with his hands as he prepared falsehood, and himself straightway said roundly: ‘I have not seen them: I have not heard of them: no man has told me of them. I could not tell you of them, nor win the reward of telling.’” When he had so spoken, Phoebus Apollo sat down. But Hermes on his part answered and said, pointing at the Son of Cronos, the lord of all the gods: “Zeus, my father, indeed I will speak truth to you; for I am truthful and I cannot tell a lie. He came to our house to-day looking for his shambling cows, as the sun was newly rising. He brought no witnesses with him nor any of the blessed gods who had seen the theft, but with great violence ordered me to confess, threatening much to throw me into wide Tartarus. For he has the rich bloom of glorious youth, while I was born but yesterday —as he too knows —, nor am I like a cattle-lifter, a sturdy fellow. Believe my tale (for you claim to be my own father), that I did not drive his cows to my house —so may I prosper—
segments.zh: 一隻銳眼的鷹也窺不見他。他用雙手揉搓雙眼，準備著謊言，隨即爽快地說道：「我沒有看見他們，我沒有聽說過他們，沒有人告訴我他們的事。我無法向你述說他們，也贏不得述說的報酬。」」他說完這些話後，福波斯阿波羅坐了下來。赫爾墨斯這邊回答說，指向克洛諾斯之子，眾神之主：「宙斯，我的父親啊，我確實要對你說真話，因為我誠實無欺，無法撒謊。他今天來到我們的家尋找他那些蹣跚的牛群，當太陽剛升起的時候。他沒有帶任何見證人來，也沒有帶任何看到失竊的有福的神靈，反而用大暴力命令我認罪，威脅說要把我扔進廣闊的塔爾塔羅斯。因為他擁有光榮青春的豐盛绽放，而我昨天才出生——如他也知道的——，我也不像一個牲畜盜賊，一個魁梧的傢伙。相信我的話吧（因為你聲稱是我親生的父親），我沒有把他的牛群趕到我的家裡——願我安康——

segments.en: nor crossed the threshold: this I say truly. I reverence Helios greatly and the other gods, and you I love and him I dread. You yourself know that I am not guilty: and I will swear a great oath upon it:—No! by these rich-decked porticoes of the gods. And some day I will punish him, strong as he is, for this pitiless inquisition; but now do you help the younger.” So spake the Cyllenian, the Slayer of Argus, while he kept shooting sidelong glances and kept his swaddling-clothes upon his arm, and did not cast them away. But Zeus laughed out loud to see his evil-plotting child well and cunningly denying guilt about the cattle. And he bade them both to be of one mind and search for the cattle, and guiding Hermes to lead the way and, without mischievousness of heart, to show the place where now he had hidden the strong cattle. Then the Son of Cronos bowed his head: and goodly Hermes obeyed him; for the will of Zeus who holds the aegis easily prevailed with him. Then the two all-glorious children of Zeus hastened both to sandy Pylos, and reached the ford of Alpheus, and came to the fields and the high-roofed byre
segments.zh: 也沒有跨過門檻：這我真誠地說。我非常尊敬赫利俄斯和其他的神靈，而你我愛，他我懼。你自己知道我是無辜的，我將為此發下偉大的誓言：——不！以這些神靈製作精美的門廊為誓。將來有一天我會懲罰他，儘管他強大，為了這無情的盤問；但現在請你幫助這年輕者吧。」基萊涅之子、殺死阿爾戈斯者如此說著，一邊射出斜眼的眼神，一邊把搖籃布裹著他的臂膀，沒有將其拋開。但宙斯大聲笑了起來，見到他那邪惡籌劃的孩子如此巧妙而機智地否認關於牛群的罪責。他命令他們兩人心意一致並搜尋牛群，引導赫爾墨斯帶路，不懷惡意之心，指出他現在隱藏那些強壯牛群的地方。那麼克洛諾斯之子點了點頭：而好的赫爾墨斯服從了他；因為持盾牌的宙斯之意志輕易地在他身上佔了上風。那麼宙斯的兩位全榮耀的孩子都匆匆趕向多沙的皮洛斯，到達了阿爾菲烏斯河的淺灘，來到了田野和高頂的牛棚

Now while Hermes went to the cave in the rock and began to drive out the strong cattle, the son of Leto, looking aside, saw the cowhides on the sheer rock. And he asked glorious Hermes at once: “How were you able, you crafty rogue, to flay two cows, new-born and babyish as you are? For my part, I dread the strength that will be yours: there is no need you should keep growing long, Cyllenian, son of Maia!” So saying, Apollo twisted strong withes with his hands and began to grow at once from the ground beneath their feet in that very place. And intertwining with one another, they quickly grew and covered all the wild-roving cattle by the will of thievish Hermes, so that Apollo was astonished as he gazed. Then the strong slayer of Argus looked furtively upon the ground with eyes flashing fire desiring to hide Very easily he softened the son of all-glorious Leto as he would, stern though the Far-shooter was. He took the lyre upon his left arm and tried each string in turn with the key, so that at his touch
segments.zh: 那裡牲畜在夜間被飼養。現在當赫爾墨斯走進岩石中的洞穴並開始趕出強壯的牛群時，勒托之子看向一旁，看到了陡峭岩石上的牛皮。他立刻問著光榮的赫爾墨斯：「你這狡詐的無賴，你怎麼能夠，新生和稚嫩如你，剝掉兩頭牛的皮？我這邊很懼怕你將擁有的力量：不需要你繼續成長了，基萊涅之子，瑪亞之子！」這樣說著，阿波羅用他的雙手扭轉強壯的柳枝，並立刻開始從地面生長，就在那非常的地點，他們的腳下。相互纏繞著，它們迅速生長並遮蔽了所有野性漂泊的牛群，以盜賊赫爾墨斯的意志，使得阿波羅看著時為之驚愕。那麼強壯的殺死阿爾戈斯者用閃閃發光的眼睛畏縮地看著地面，渴望隱藏。非常輕易地他柔化了全榮耀之子勒托，如他所願，儘管遠射者很嚴厲。他把豎琴拿到左臂上，輪流試著每一根弦，用琴撥，使得在他的觸碰下

segments.en: it sounded awesomely. And Phoebus Apollo laughed for joy; for the sweet throb of the marvellous music went to his heart, and a soft longing took hold on his soul as he listened. Then the son of Maia, harping sweetly upon his lyre, took courage and stood at the left hand of Phoebus Apollo; and soon, while he played shrilly on his lyre, he lifted up his voice and sang, and lovely was the sound of his voice that followed. He sang the story of the deathless gods and of the dark earth, how at the first they came to be, and how each one received his portion. First among the gods he honored Mnemosyne, mother of the Muses, in his song; for the son of Maia was of her following. And next the goodly son of Zeus hymned the rest of the immortals according to their order in age, and told how each was born, mentioning all in order as he struck the lyre upon his arm. But Apollo was seized with a longing not to be allayed, and he opened his mouth and spoke winged words to Hermes: “Slayer of oxen, trickster, busy one, comrade of the feast, this song of yours is worth fifty cows, and I believe that presently we shall settle our quarrel peacefully. But come now, tell me this, resourceful son of Maia:
segments.zh: 聲音迴響駭人。遠射者阿波羅為之欣然而笑；那甜蜜而奇妙的音樂震顫直達他心間，柔和的渴望在他聽時佔據了他的靈魂。那時邁亞之子手撥豎琴，甜美地鳴奏著，鼓起勇氣站到了遠射者阿波羅的左側；旋即他在豎琴上尖銳地彈奏著，揚起嗓音唱歌，他隨之而起的聲音是甘美的。他唱不死的神祇與黑暗的大地，唱它們初時如何生成，各個如何獲得份額。眾神中他首先在歌中敬頌了謨涅摩敘涅，繆斯之母；因為邁亞之子從屬於她。隨後宙斯的優美之子依照年歲次序讚頌其餘的永生者，敍述各自如何誕生，在手臂上撥動豎琴時將各個逐一提及。但阿波羅被難以遏止的渴望所捕獲，他張開嘴唇向赫爾墨斯說出有翅的言語：「屠牛者、騙子、忙碌者、筵席的同伴，你這首歌值五十頭母牛，我相信我們不久就能和平地解決我們的爭執。但來吧，告訴我這個，機靈的邁亞之子：

segments.greek:

νῦν γάρ τοι κλέος ἔσται ἐν ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσι
σοί τʼ αὐτῷ καὶ μητρί· τὸ δʼ ἀτρεκέως ἀγορεύσω·
segments.en: has this marvellous thing been with you from your birth, or did some god or mortal man give it you —a noble gift —and teach you heavenly song? For wonderful is this new-uttered sound I hear, the like of which I vow that no man nor god dwelling on Olympus ever yet has known but you,O thievish son of Maia. What skill is this? What song for desperate cares? What way of song? For verily here are three things to hand all at once from which to choose, —mirth, and love, and sweet sleep. And though I am a follower of the Olympian Muses who love dances and the bright path of song —the full-toned chant and ravishing thrill of flutes —yet I never cared for any of those feats of skill at young men's revels, as I do now for this: I am filled with wonder, O son of Zeus, at your sweet playing. But now, since you, though little, have such glorious skill, sit down, dear boy, and respect the words of your elders For now you shall have renown among the deathless gods, you and your mother also. This I will declare to you exactly:
segments.zh: 這奇妙之物自你誕生以來就與你同在，還是某位神祇或凡人給予了它——一件高貴的禮物——並教會你天上的歌謠？ 這新出世的聲音是多麼奇異啊，我據此發誓，無論是凡人還是奧林匹斯上的神，除了你之外，誰都未曾知曉，啊，盜賊之子邁亞之子。這是什麼技藝？什麼歌曲可解絕望之心？什麼樣的歌法？ 確實這兒同時備有三樣可供選擇的東西——歡樂、愛戀與甘美的睡眠。雖然我是追隨奧林匹斯繆斯的人，她們摯愛舞蹈與歌謠的光輝之路——飽滿的吟唱與長笛的奪魄之音——然而我從未在少年歡宴上介意過這些技藝之舉，如我現在為這個而介意的那樣：我為你的甜蜜彈奏而充滿驚嘆，啊，宙斯之子。但現在，既然你雖然年小卻擁有如此輝煌的技藝，請坐下，親愛的男孩，尊敬你長輩的言語。如今你將在不死的神祇中獲得聲譽，你和你的母親也將如此。我會這樣確切地宣告給你：

segments.en: by this shaft of cornel wood I will surely make you a leader renowned among the deathless gods, and fortunate, and will give you glorious gifts and will not deceive you from first to last.” Then Hermes answered him with artful words: “You question me carefully, O Far-worker; yet I am not jealous that you should enter upon my art: this day you shall know it. For I seek to be friendly with you both in thought and word. Now you well know all things in your heart, since you sit foremost among the deathless gods, O son of Zeus, and are goodly and strong. And wise Zeus loves you as all right is, and has given you splendid gifts. And they say that from the utterance of Zeus you have learned both the honors due to the gods, O Far-worker, and oracles from Zeus, even all his ordinances. Of all these I myself have already learned that you have great wealth. Now, you are free to learn whatever you please; but since, as it seems, your heart is so strongly set on playing the lyre, chant, and play upon it, and give yourself to merriment, taking this as a gift from me, and do you, my friend, bestow glory on me. Sing well with this clear-voiced companion in your hands; for you are skilled in good, well-ordered utterance.
segments.zh: 藉著這根山茱萸木的箭杆，我必然使你成為不死的神祇中聲譽卓著的領袖，幸運而富有的，並將賜你輝煌的禮物，自始至終不會欺騙你。」隨後赫爾墨斯用工於言詞的話語回答他說：「你詰問我甚勤，啊，遠射者；然而我並不嫉妒你進入我的技藝：今日你將認識它。因為我尋求與你友善，無論在心意還是言語。現在你在你心中洞悉一切，既然你坐在不死的神祇之首位，啊，宙斯之子，英俊而強健。智慧的宙斯愛你如理應所為，並賜予你光輝的禮物。他們說從宙斯的啟示中你學得了神祇應受的敬重，啊，遠射者，以及來自宙斯的神諭，所有他的制度。我自己已然得知，你在這些事中擁有巨大的財富。現在，你可以自由地學習任何你所想要的；然而既然似乎你的心如此堅決地傾向於撥動豎琴、吟唱與彈奏，就請把自己投入歡樂，拿著這個作為我的禮物，而你，我的朋友，應將榮耀賜予我。用這位清亮嗓音的同伴在你手中好好地唱歌；因為你擅長美好而井然有序的表達。

νῆις ἐὼν τὸ πρῶτον ἐπιζαφελῶς ἐρεείνῃ,

segments.en: From now on bring it confidently to the rich feast and lovely dance and glorious revel, a joy by night and by day. Whoso with wit and wisdom enquires of it cunningly, him it teaches through its sound all manner of things that delight the mind, being easily played with gentle familiarities, for it abhors toilsome drudgery; but whoso in ignorance enquires of it violently, to him it chatters mere vanity and foolishness. But you are able to learn whatever you please. So then, I will give you this lyre, glorious son of Zeus, while I for my part will graze down with wild-roving cattle the pastures on hill and horse-feeding plain: so shall the cows covered by the bulls calve abundantly both males and females. And now there is no need for you, bargainer though you are, to be furiously angry.” When Hermes had said this, he held out the lyre: and Phoebus Apollo took it, and readily put his shining whip in Hermes' hand, and ordained him keeper of herds. The son of Maia received it joyfully,
segments.zh: 從此以後，將它自信地帶到豐盛的盛宴、可愛的舞蹈和光榮的狂歡去，日夜都是喜悅。凡是以機智和智慧巧妙地向它詢問的人，它就通過它的聲音教給他種種悅人心意的事物，因為它易於彈奏，親暱溫和，厭惡勞苦的苦役；但凡是無知地蠻力向它詢問的人，它就只向他喋喋不休地吐露虛妄和愚蠢。但你能夠學會凡是你所願意學的。那麼，我就把這竪琴給你，宙斯的光榮之子，而我自己將放牧野遊的牛群，在山丘和良馬出產的平原上吃草：這樣，母牛們被公牛覆蓋就會產下許多公牛犢和母牛犢。現在對於你這個討價還價的人，就再也沒有必要怒火衝天了。」赫爾墨斯說完這些話，就遞出了竪琴：斐波斯阿波羅接過了它，欣然把自己閃耀的鞭子放在赫爾墨斯的手中，並任命他為牛群的守護者。邁亞之子高興地收下了它，

Λητοΐδην ἐφίλησε διαμπερὲς ὡς ἔτι καὶ νῦν,

καὶ τότε Λητοΐδης Ἑρμῆν πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε·
δείδια, Μαιάδος υἱέ, διάκτορε, ποικιλομῆτα,
μή μοι ἅμα κλέψῃς κίθαριν καὶ καμπύλα τόξα·
τιμὴν γὰρ πὰρ Ζηνὸς ἔχεις ἐπαμοίβια ἔργα
θήσειν ἀνθρώποισι κατὰ χθόνα πουλυβότειραν.
ἀλλʼ εἴ μοι τλαίης γε θεῶν μέγαν ὅρκον ὀμόσσαι,
ἢ κεφαλῇ νεύσας ἢ ἐπὶ Στυγὸς ὄβριμον ὕδωρ,
segments.en: while the glorious son of Leto, the lord far-working Apollo, took the lyre upon his left arm and tried each string with the key. Awesomely it sounded at the touch of the god, while he sang sweetly to its note. Afterwards they two, the all-glorious sons of Zeus turned the cows back towards the sacred meadow, but themselves hastened back to snowy Olympus, delighting in the lyre. Then wise Zeus was glad and made them both friends. And Hermes loved the son of Leto continually, even as he does now, when he had given the lyre as token to the Far-shooter, who played it skilfully, holding it upon his arm. But for himself Hermes found out another cunning art and made himself the pipes whose sound is heard afar. Whosoever shall come guided by the call and flight of birds of sure omen, that man shall have advantage through my voice, and I will not deceive him. But whoso shall trust to idly-chattering birds and shall seek to invoke my prophetic art contrary to my will, and to understand more than the eternal gods, I declare that he shall come on an idle journey; yet his gifts I would take.
